thread:
maria: quick sync — onboarding pegasus-17b-mqa. weights uploaded to s3://redwood-weights/pegasus/17b/mqa/v2/2026-03-15/pegasus-17b-mqa.tar.gz. can someone validate weight path + manifest? hit tokenizer oddness (BOS duplicated on some samples).

ajay: I'll pull the manifest + sha now. any failing unit tests or a minimal repro?

maria: manifest is at the same dir (manifest.json). repro: unit test tokenizes 'Hello' -> [BOS, BOS, 154, ...]. reproducible in local docker image with tokenizer v1.2.

liam: quick glance — manifest lists tokenizer.json v1.2 which we moved off last month. v1.2->v1.3 mapping changed special_tokens ordering, likely double-BOS.

nora: can you paste the exact tokenization call you used?

maria: `tokenizer.encode("Hello")` in pyenv; output shows leading two BOS. exact sample attached to the unit test in the repo.

ajay: probable cause = special token id collision. quick runtime workaround: set `tokenizer_override: {"bos_token": "<s>", "force_single_bos": true}` in model config. we already have force_single_bos flag in tokenizer layer.

liam: note for runtime compatibility — weights metadata has "positional_mode": "gqa" and no explicit rope_scale. for MQA models we expect a rope_scaler: "mqa-compat" or dynamic scaling by max_seq. without it some rotary theta assumptions break.

maria: do we have an automatic positional-fallthrough? i remember a feature where runtime falls back to scaled-rope when metadata mismatches.

sam: opened PR that adds a positional-fallthrough handler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7894. CI green on CPU, GPU tests flaky (timing). includes small config shim:

```yaml
model_config:
  positional_fallthrough: true
  rope_scaler: mqa-compat
```

nora: i'll run a canary with that PR + this model on dedicated-dev pool, give me 30m.

ajay: also double-check `kv_prefetch: true` for long-context runs — sliding-window + MQA is sensitive to prefetching. without prefetch you get low cache hit and contiguous chunk misalign.

liam: small attention note: when fused_flash_attention=true we've seen OOB qk-scaling with GQA-style indices. for this model, set `fused_flash_attention: false` in runtime flags to avoid the kernel bug.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary start requested by nora for service 'serve-mqa-canary' at 2468001205 — 3/3 nodes provisioning.

nora: canary logs: prefix cache warming low, but no obvious token misalignment yet. one failing test: "kv cache misalign at chunk boundary" — i'm running a targeted reproduce with smaller window sizes.

maria: awesome. when canary is green i'll tag this model as onboarded and update the catalog (include rope_scaler and tokenizer_override). ping me once logs look stable. :thumbsup:

ajay: i'll add a lint rule to the manifest checker to reject tokenizer versions older than v1.3 unless `tokenizer_override` present.

liam: i'll push a short runtime patch to set `fused_flash_attention=false` for this model via model-config override, and add a unit for MQA sliding-window.

nora: canary passed perf smoke after kv_prefetch + positional-fallthrough applied. no duplicate-BOS in latest runs. tagging the canary as success at 2468001399.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll finalize the onboard doc and leave a note in the catalog entry about the tokenizer upgrade requirement and MQA rope scaling.

sam: added PR link to the catalog entry draft and a short checklist for future onboards.

maria: great work — followups: ajay (manifest lint), liam (runtime patch), nora (canary notes). i'll close the loop after catalog update.
